_comment: CHOICE — several pictures of ONE thing, and he picks one (or None of these / Other).
This is the shape for 'here are three designs of the same row'. Never give each design its own Yes/No step: that asks him the same question three times and lets him say yes to two of them.
The pictures come from the deck's LAST run, so one sweep of a workbench holding every candidate is enough.
title: The send button — three designs, pick one
_comment_title: title: what this deck is about, in his words.
_comment_key: key: a short name for this deck. His pick is saved under it.
_comment_out: out: the page build writes, beside this spec.
_comment_images: images: where the cropped pictures land. It must contain this file's own name.

runs._comment: runs: one sweep is enough — every design was captured in the same run of the workbench.

_comment_themes: themes: when the choice is about shape, not colour, one palette keeps him on the question.

crops._comment: crops (optional): regions this deck needs that crops.json does not have. Each is [which capture plan, which shot, WIDTHxHEIGHT+X+Y] on the 1440x900 shots. A design that only exists in your workbench needs one of these per candidate.

steps._comment: One step, one question, every design under it. Two designs minimum.
steps._comment_id: id: your name for this question. It labels his answer.
steps._comment_surface: surface: the part of the app this lives in, named the way he would name it.
steps.path: The row under the message box
steps._comment_path: path: how he would get there.
steps.headline: Which send button should the message box use?
steps._comment_headline: headline: the question itself, in one sentence. 25 words at most, no code words.
steps.notice: Whichever you pick becomes the button on every screen that sends a message.
steps._comment_notice: notice (optional): what riding on the pick — where it shows up, what else it changes.
steps.risk: All three keep the same place on screen, so nothing moves whichever you pick.
steps._comment_risk: risk (optional): the Risk card, shared by every design. Per-design risks go on the design.

variants._comment: One design. Its picture, its name, and the sentence that sells it.
variants._comment_id: id: your name for this design. It is what his answer records, so make it readable.
variants.label: Arrow only
variants._comment_label: label: the design's name, two or three words. Never write '(recommended)' here — there is no such flag on a choice; say it in the summary.
variants._comment_crop: crop: this design's own picture. Every design needs one.
variants.summary: An arrow in a circle, no words. The smallest of the three.
variants._comment_summary: summary: one or two sentences on what this design is and what it costs.
variants._comment_measured: measured (optional): a number that separates it from the others. Needs a digit in it.
variants.risk: New users have to guess what the arrow does.
variants._comment_risk: risk (optional): what is wrong with THIS design in particular.

variants.label: Arrow and the word Send
variants.summary: The arrow with 'Send' beside it. Reads at a glance, takes more room.

highlight._comment: highlight (optional on a design): box one part of this picture. Leave it out and the whole picture is the point.

variants.label: Full-width bar
variants.summary: A bar across the whole width under the message box. Impossible to miss, and it pushes everything else down.
variants.risk: Takes a line of room away from the message you are writing.

steps._comment: A second question, at its smallest: two designs, one line each. Everything else on a design is optional.
steps.path: The strip along the bottom of the window
steps.headline: How should the branch name be shortened when it does not fit?

variants.label: Cut the middle
variants.summary: Keeps the start and the end, with a gap between them.

variants.label: Cut the end
variants.summary: Keeps the start only, like a file name that runs out of room.
